clue.text: Change made by Michael Butor

definitions.meaning: an alteration or adjustment to something
The 1957 novel by the French writer Michel Butor, here printed Michael

explanation.surface: Someone notes an alteration the French novelist made.
explanation.walkthrough: Butor's book is usually known in English as Second Thoughts, but its French title is the word wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: An alteration is a synonym for a change, and Butor's novel carries that word as its title.

clue.text: Novelist preparing for action

definitions.meaning: Olivia ..., author of the Balkan Trilogy
crew taking their stations, as in staffing the guns of a ship

explanation.surface: A writer is getting ready for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivia Manning wrote the Balkan and Levant trilogies; to staff guns or posts with crew is the verb's sense of readying for action.

clue.text: Pamela Frankenau's is proverbially better

parts.note: Pamela Frankau (printed Frankenau) wrote The ... We Know, and the proverb says the one we know is better than the one we don't

explanation.surface: A novelist's work is said to be superior.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'better the devil you know' supplies the fiend, and Frankau's novel title The Devil We Know echoes it.

clue.text: Translation of Fraser oft attributed to Francis Brett Young

indicators.note: a translation renders words into a new form, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rendered a work by Fraser that was credited to another novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translation of' rearranges FRASER OFT; Francis Brett Young, an English novelist of the Worcestershire borders, wrote Far Forest (1936).
explanation.definitionFit: Far Forest is a 1936 novel by Francis Brett Young, so a book credited to him fits.

clue.text: Hughes's flier was also war reporter

definitions.meaning: Ted Hughes's 1970 poem sequence is named after a black bird
the black carrion bird haunts battlefields and in legend (the Irish war goddess Morrigan) announces war

explanation.surface: A poet's pilot also covered a war for a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Ted Hughes's poetic trickster is a black bird, and that bird is a traditional herald of battle and slaughter.

clue.text: Thomas's powerless treatment of Greene theme?

definitions.meaning: Edward Thomas wrote a poem with this title
Graham Greene's novel The Power and ... with 'The Power and' removed

explanation.surface: A Welsh writer handled one of Greene's subjects without any force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powerless' means strip 'The Power and' from Greene's title The Power and the Glory, leaving the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Thomas's poem bears this title, and it is also what is left of Greene's novel title once the power is gone.

clue.text: Abstract style originates only partly as realist tendency

indicators.note: where each of the following words originates is its start, so their opening letters are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A non-figurative movement grew partly out of realism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originates' takes the first letters of 'only partly as realist tendency'; the surface reads them as a description of art history.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s abstract movement using optical illusions of line and colour.

clue.text: Some extremely precious writing

parts.note: precious here means affected and overwrought, as in John Lyly's elaborate Elizabethan prose

explanation.surface: A piece of writing is very valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precious' suggests valuable, but here it means affectedly refined; the style is named from Lyly's Euphues.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a highly ornate, artificial prose style modelled on John Lyly's Euphues.

clue.text: Something hidden from E. Phillips Oppenheim and Laurence Binyon

definitions.meaning: a thing kept out of sight or knowledge

definitions.text: from E. Phillips Oppenheim and Laurence Binyon
definitions.meaning: both writers published a work with The ... as its title

explanation.surface: Something has been concealed from two writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' looks like 'kept away from', but it means 'written by': Oppenheim's novel and Binyon's poems share the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept concealed is a confidence, and the word is the title of works by both writers.

clue.text: Postponement sine die threatened by large corvid

definitions.meaning: sine die means without a fixed day, so the postponement is for ever
the raven in Poe's poem repeats its ominous single word

explanation.surface: An indefinite adjournment is menaced by a big black bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting something off without any date means it will happen at no future time; Poe's raven croaks that very word.

clue.text: Entertain artist's inspiration

definitions.meaning: to divert or make laugh
a goddess or person who inspires a creator, read as two words, a muse

explanation.surface: An artist's muse keeps people diverted.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert someone is a synonym; split as A MUSE it is a creator's source of inspiration.

clue.text: "Things — - — had ever bad success" (Henry VI Part 3)

definitions.text: "Things — - — had ever bad success" (Henry VI Part 3)

parts.words: "Things — - — had ever bad success" (Henry VI Part 3)
parts.note: the line in Shakespeare's play says that things obtained dishonestly never prosper

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in the line from Henry VI Part 3, Act 2 Scene 2: dishonestly acquired gains never end well.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquired by wrongful means, which Shakespeare's line says never turns out well.

clue.text: Munitions manufacturer and collaborator produced dramatic results

definitions.meaning: a maker of arrows, the munitions of archery
John ... co-wrote plays with Francis Beaumont and with Shakespeare

explanation.surface: An arms maker and his partner put on a sensational show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Munitions' suggests shells, but the weapons are arrows; 'dramatic' is literal, plays for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow-maker is the old trade name, and John Fletcher was the Jacobean dramatist who partnered Beaumont.

clue.text: Song he composed in land of plenty

indicators.note: a composed piece is put together, so the letters of the two words are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: He wrote a song in a rich country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' fits the song but rearranges SONG HE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this region of Egypt was the fertile land given to Joseph's family, so it stands for abundance.

clue.text: Poliakoff and Potter are well-known ones

definitions.text: Poliakoff and Potter are well-known ones

parts.words: Poliakoff and Potter are well-known ones
parts.note: the playwright Poliakoff and the humorist Potter share a first name

explanation.surface: Two writers are famous examples of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Dennis Potter is the famous television Potter, but Stephen Potter wrote Gamesmanship; both men here share the first name Stephen.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Poliakoff and Stephen Potter are two notable bearers of that first name.

clue.text: Engraving of laconic fieldsman

parts.note: laconic means terse, and dry humour is understated
point is a cricket fielding position square of the batsman on the off side

explanation.surface: A picture etched by a fielder of few words.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, point is a fielding position near the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an intaglio print made by scratching a plate directly with a needle.

clue.text: Nursery rep, company?

definitions.meaning: a pre-school where small children play
a repertory company is a troupe that performs plays

explanation.surface: Children's room question about a theatre company.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-school for toddlers; split, it is a band of actors staging plays, like a repertory troupe.

clue.text: How Oscar Wilde felt we should be, from laughing, reading of Little Nell's death

definitions.text: How Oscar Wilde felt we should be, from laughing, reading of Little Nell's death

parts.words: How Oscar Wilde felt we should be, from laughing, reading of Little Nell's death
parts.note: Wilde said one must have a heart of stone to read the death of Little Nell without laughing, so readers' eyes would be wet with tears of mirth

explanation.surface: Wilde's famous joke about Dickens's sentimental deathbed scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual sense is sentimental tears, but Wilde's readers weep from laughing at The Old Curiosity Shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist with tears, here tears of laughter rather than of sorrow.

clue.text: His arrival and departure were booked in 1943

definitions.text: His arrival and departure were booked in 1943

parts.words: His arrival and departure were booked in 1943
parts.note: Arrival and Departure is a 1943 novel, so its coming and going were put in a book

explanation.surface: A traveller's journey was reserved during the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booked' suggests a travel reservation; it means published as a book, Arthur Koestler's novel Arrival and Departure.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Koestler, Hungarian-born writer, published the novel Arrival and Departure in 1943.

clue.text: Composer is a different lady, OK?

indicators.note: different means made other than before, so the letters of the words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is fine that the composer is another woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Different' rearranges LADY OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoltan Kodaly was a Hungarian composer and music educator.

clue.text: Dragon-killer no gentleman, getting a certain amount back

parts.note: a cad is an ill-mannered man, the opposite of a gentleman

indicators.note: back means the word for an amount is written in reverse order

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: A dragon-slayer behaves badly and gets money returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns SUM round to MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Cadmus killed the dragon guarding a spring and sowed its teeth before founding Thebes.

clue.text: "She came. And sang to me the whole / Of those three — that you made" (Tennyson)

definitions.text: "She came. And sang to me the whole / Of those three — that you made" (Tennyson)

parts.words: "She came. And sang to me the whole / Of those three — that you made" (Tennyson)
parts.note: the missing word in the lines from Maud is the verses of the song she sang

explanation.surface: A quotation from Tennyson with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in the lines from Tennyson's Maud: the three units of verse that were sung.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of lines of verse, three of which she sang in the passage from Tennyson's Maud.

clue.text: Two notes added to any I composed for Hungarian pianist

parts.note: doh is the first note of the tonic sol-fa scale

indicators.note: 'to' puts one piece inside the other
composed means put together, so the letters of the words any I are set in an arrangement, here the order printed

parts.note: n. is the standard abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A pianist wrote music for the Hungarian.
explanation.walkthrough: The two notes are DOH (sol-fa) and N (the abbreviation for a footnote), put before ANY I; 'composed' leaves those letters in the order printed. Ernst von Dohnanyi was a Hungarian pianist and composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernst von Dohnanyi was a celebrated Hungarian pianist, conductor and composer.

clue.text: Scene of conflict in Shakespeare, naturally

indicators.note: in means the letters run inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Fighting naturally occurs in Shakespeare's plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the letters running across 'Shakespeare, naturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium or ring where combatants meet, and figuratively any field of struggle.

clue.text: Character in Eliot drama, also found in saga that inspired it

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A figure in Eliot's play also appears in the ancient story behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' signals letters across 'saga that'; Eliot's The Family Reunion reworks Aeschylus's Oresteia.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha is the aunt in T. S. Eliot's verse play The Family Reunion.

clue.text: Attempt by Charlotte M. Yonge

definitions.meaning: an effort or test
Charlotte M. Yonge wrote the novel The ... (1864)

explanation.surface: An effort made by a Victorian novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: A try or test is a synonym for an attempt, and Yonge's sequel to The Daisy Chain bears the word as its title.

clue.text: A French refusal for prolific writer

explanation.surface: A Frenchman says no to a productive author.
explanation.walkthrough: The anonymous author is credited with countless poems and sayings, so is called prolific.
explanation.definitionFit: Works of unknown authorship are credited to this abbreviation of anonymous, making it the most productive name in print.

clue.text: Weapon accompanying a lot at the Round Table

definitions.meaning: a long spear carried by a mounted knight

definitions.text: accompanying a lot at the Round Table
definitions.meaning: put with the word lot it makes the name of Arthur's knight Lancelot

explanation.surface: A weapon goes with a lot of knights at Arthur's table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' looks like many people, but it is the word 'lot' that the weapon joins to name the knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight's spear; joined with LOT it gives Lancelot of the Round Table.

clue.text: American reportedly with zero intelligence is in fact a brilliant playwright

parts.note: Yank is a slang word for an American
zero looks like the letter O

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for intelligence is heard, not seen

explanation.surface: A dim American turns out to be a gifted dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' makes WITS sound as WITZ; Susan Yankowitz is an American playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan Yankowitz is an American dramatist known for Night Sky and work with the Open Theater.

clue.text: Catalan dance might be Paul's in Delacroix subject

parts.note: the sardana is the circle dance of Catalonia

indicators.note: might be means the letters of the name could be rearranged into another form

parts.note: the name with its possessive s

explanation.surface: A Catalan dance may belong to Paul in a painter's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might be' rearranges PAULS into PALUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Delacroix painted The Death of Sardanapalus (1827), the Assyrian king on his funeral pyre.
